page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-8-highlssd is a memory-optimized and storage-focused server instance belonging to the z3 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. This instance is equipped with 64 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a single local NVMe SSD providing 3221 GB of capacity, while no dedicated GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations place the z3-highmem-8-highlssd consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core Geekbench score of 1694.0 and a multi-core score of 6517.0, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 544.21 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 53.42 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 33.03 GB/sec. Database operations under Passmark score at 3908.44, and the system processes Redis SET operations at a rate of 8.92 million operations per second.

The hardware profile offers high resource density by combining a substantial 3221 GB local NVMe SSD with 64 GB of RAM, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space and large memory footprints without the overhead of external storage. However, performance tradeoffs exist in complex computational tasks. While the instance handles prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model at 55.98 tokens per second, text generation for the same model drops to a weak tier at 7.36 tokens per second, and large 70B models are unsupported. This server is configured for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads such as database hosting, caching layers, data processing, and localized file serving.
